chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a contracted slave (mukatab) who killed a man in error, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him from his blood money (diyah) is in proportion to what has been freed of his debt, and upon his master is what remains from the value of the slave. So if the contracted slave is unable (to pay), there is no blood-money guarantors (aqilah) for him; rather, that is upon the Imam of the Muslims.

key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The Imam of the Muslims, who assumes financial responsibility in this case
key_terms.دِيَتِهِ: His blood money or compensation for killing
key_terms.عَاقِلَتَهُ: The group of male relatives responsible for paying blood money
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has a contract with his master to pay a certain sum for his freedom

ai.seo_question: How is blood money divided for a contracted slave who commits accidental homicide?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a unique jurisprudential ruling where the blood money liability for a mukatab (contracted slave) is proportionally divided between the slave and his master based on the slave's emancipation progress. It notably excludes the traditional tribal guarantors (aqilah), assigning the residual burden directly to the Imam, which underscores the Imam's role as the ultimate financial authority in the absence of tribal structures. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam's comprehensive responsibility for justice and compensation in complex social hierarchies.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding a contracted slave who killed a man in error. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him from his wergild, is in proportion to what he is free, and upon his master is what remains from the value of the price. So if the contracted slave is frustrated (from paying), so there is no blood (compensation) for him. But rather, that is upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> of the Muslims’.
